svg.aria-label: The two-minute thread-safety answer template, worked once on making FundsLedger.reserveStake thread-safe, as five sequential frames. Frame 1 states the invariant: a StakeSplit's bonusPortion plus cashPortion must exactly equal the stake, drawing from CLIENT_BONUS_AVAILABLE before CLIENT_CASH_AVAILABLE. Frame 2 states the policy: locking, because confinement and immutability are both ruled out. Frame 3 states the mechanism: a ReentrantLock per client id held across the read-check-write. Frame 4 states the cost: serialized reservations per client against a 1,200 reservations per second platform-wide load. Frame 5 states the accepted failure mode: possible stall under a slow call, but not deadlock, since there is exactly one lock per client.
svg.text: THE TWO-MINUTE THREAD-SAFETY ANSWER TEMPLATE
Worked example: make FundsLedger.reserveStake thread-safe
FRAME 1 — STATE THE INVARIANT
"The invariant: a StakeSplit's bonusPortion plus cashPortion must exactly equal the stake —
a 3.33 stake always splits as 0.33 bonus + 3.00 cash, drawing from CLIENT_BONUS_AVAILABLE
before CLIENT_CASH_AVAILABLE, and neither available balance may go negative."
change: nothing yet — this is the fixed point every later beat must preserve
FRAME 2 — STATE THE POLICY
"The policy: confinement is out — reserveStake is called concurrently from multiple request
threads for the same client. Immutability is out too — the wallet's available balances are
mutated on every call. So the policy is locking: serialize every reserveStake per client."
change: from what must hold to what discipline enforces it — confinement and immutability ruled out first
FRAME 3 — STATE THE MECHANISM
"The mechanism: a ReentrantLock per client id, held across the read-check-write of
CLIENT_BONUS_AVAILABLE and CLIENT_CASH_AVAILABLE and the write of the StakeSplit —
acquired at the top of reserveStake, released in a finally block."
change: the policy becomes a concrete API — try/finally around ReentrantLock.lock()/unlock()
FRAME 4 — STATE THE COST
"The cost: every reserveStake for the same client now serializes. QuizStakes runs at
1,200 reservations/sec platform-wide, so a client with unusually high stake volume
becomes a lock-contention hotspot, and every acquisition adds latency under load."
change: names the price of the mechanism — per-client throughput, not platform-wide throughput
FRAME 5 — STATE THE FAILURE MODE YOU ACCEPT
"The failure mode I accept: if the lock is ever held across a slow call — I/O, a downstream
request — threads queue up behind one client's lock and stall. I accept that because the
critical section is memory-only. I do not accept deadlock: there is exactly one lock per
client, and reserveStake never holds two clients' locks at once."
change: names the trade-off explicitly instead of leaving it implied — stall accepted, deadlock engineered out
frame number badge
frame panel — one beat's spoken sentence(s) + what changed since the last frame
A → B : frame A is spoken, then frame B follows in the same two-minute answer
